  * 【涉及范围与推进】英伟达后续将在华盛顿政策与开源模型生态扩张中维持高频介入。

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in Nvidia's decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend, convinced he alone protected American-made open-weight AI models, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.
  > Open-weight AI models are systems whose core components are publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific tasks. Their growth has become a major business opportunity for Nvidia because they broaden demand for the company's chips and computing infrastructure beyond a handful of large AI developers.
  > China leads in the development of open-weight AI systems, which are gaining ground with US companies because they can be cheaper than proprietary AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic . They can also perform nearly as well.
  > Nvidia has been one of the most prominent backers of the US open-weight ecosystem. Nvidia in August agreed to buy the company Hugging Face, a platform that developers use to host open-weight AI models, among other AI-related resources. Nvidia is also an investor in Reflection AI, an American company that launched its first open-weight model in October.
  > Huang and Nvidia's lobbyists have also pressed US lawmakers to support the development of open-weight AI technology, with Huang writing in a letter earlier this year that they should avoid "premature restrictions" on such tools.
  > Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports that he engaged in several extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
  > Reuters reported on November 18 that the Trump administration was considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, including open-weight models, as part of an effort to reduce reliance on Chinese technology.
  > Republican lawmakers have increasingly echoed the argument that open-weight AI is critical to competing with China. Two leading House Republican lawmakers on Friday called on the Trump administration to help American companies developing open-weight AI models, adding that it would position the US to better counter China.
  > Copyright 2026 Thomson Reuters.

### xAI转型算力租赁商，Anthropic成最大租户
- 落地页链接: https://ainewsradar.xyz/zh/news/627f6e610ddcce6f
- 原始信源: Business Insider (https://www.businessinsider.com/jensen-huang-returns-to-nvidia-hq-im-terribly-sorry-2026-11)
- 核心摘要: 受限于自身模型竞争压力，xAI将重心转向算力租赁，Anthropic每月贡献31亿美元合同
- 核验事实清单:
  * 【核心事件】xAI负责人埃隆·马斯克；Anthropic（客户）在AI基础设施租赁市场：xAI裁撤部分自主模型研发，向Anthropic大规模租赁算力
  * 【起因与机理】自身模型竞争力不足，且迫于IPO后的盈利压力，转向高回报的基础设施服务
  * 【关键数据与实测】Anthropic与xAI签署每月31亿美元的算力租赁协议。
  * 【各方立场与态度】AI产业商业逻辑重构，算力资源变现能力成为衡量公司估值的核心指标。

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters Monday to cheers from employees, less than two weeks after his stunning ouster. Nvidia employees gathered at headquarters to mark the moment, chanting "Jensen! Jensen!" as he arrived back at the office, according to a person familiar with the scene.
  > The crowd was so packed that employees jostled for a glimpse. Rather than his signature black leather jacket, the source said he appeared to be wearing a navy cotton coat. Huang put his hand on his heart several times and said, "This is my first day at work," according to a video of the scene.
  > "I'm terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this." "I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around," he said, according to another person in attendance. "I don't have a computer, so the IT department is gonna give me a new PC," Huang added. In public posts, Nvidia employees flocked to social media to celebrate Huang's return to the company.
  > A "Stand with Jensen" petition calling for his reinstatement had previously garnered more than 200,000 signatures, including thousands who identified as current employees. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider. Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, reversing course just 11 days after his resignation amid revelations about his personal relationships and an ongoing investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
  > Prominent names in business also applauded Huang's reinstatement, while President Trump said he "convinced" Nvidia's board to make the decision as the company's stock had plummeted in his absence.

### Nothing's 即将推出的 Ear Note 是一对具有 AI 转录功能的耳塞
- 落地页链接: https://ainewsradar.xyz/zh/news/35ecac9c957ce63a
- 原始信源: The Verge AI (https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/1040357/nothing-ear-note-earbuds-ai-recording)
- 核心摘要: 没有什么新的人工智能设备是Ear Note，一组耳塞和配备麦克风的充电盒，可以记录和转录对话，并带有一个连接的应用程序来管理录音、转录和人工智能生成的摘要，类似于苹果的新手表功能和亚马逊的Bee可穿戴设备等设备。诺西
- 核验事实清单:
  * 【核心事件】苹果公司 (Apple Inc.)：Nothing's 即将推出的 Ear Note 是一对具有 AI 转录功能的耳塞
  * 【核心事实细节】Nothing's 即将推出的 Ear Note 是一对具有 AI 转录功能的耳塞。
  * 【行业研判】首席执行官 Carl Pei 没有表现出什么。

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to Bloomberg, but said the company hasn’t yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th.
  > The report also says Nothing’s rumored plans for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be “pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.” In a post on X, Pei said this is “the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI. Rather than ask you to carry a new product, we took something you already wear and trust and made it intelligent.”
  > According to Bloomberg, the earbuds will “support interactions with various AI agents, including a more basic voice-control system developed by Nothing, letting users engage in back-and-forth conversations.” Users will also be able to record themselves with a “Talk” button on the case, like Nothing previously included on the Ear 3, which also has recording capabilities. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

### Adyen Co 首席执行官 Pieter Van Der 将从支付公司退休
- 落地页链接: https://ainewsradar.xyz/zh/news/b84993440e3f5ceb
- 原始信源: Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-23/adyen-co-ceo-pieter-van-der-does-to-retire-from-payments-firm)
- 核心摘要: Adyen 已将其支付处理业务打造成欧洲最大的创业成功案例之一。现在，它正在悄然部署人工智能，以保持其惊人的增长势头。这家总部位于阿姆斯特丹的公司从内部而不是通过收购来构建工具的理念已经得到了认可
- 核验事实清单:
  * 【核心事件】Adyen Co 首席执行官 Pieter Van Der 将从支付公司退休
  * 【起因与机理】巨额融资意向凸显出头部模型公司在研发前沿架构与构建超级计算集群过程中巨大的资本消耗率，企业正力求在公开上市前锁定充沛流动性以构筑壁垒。
  * 【核心事实细节】Adyen在印度移动金融与大额数字支付市场。
  * 【行业研判】这家总部位于阿姆斯特丹的公司从内部而不是通过收购来构建工具的理念对其崛起至关重要。

Its risk management service -- called RevenueProtect -- includes a ShoperDNA feature, which allows for real-time identification of shoppers.
  > With AI, Adyen has been able to expand the data points and methodology, which in turn enables much more granular examination of a person or pattern when a purchase is being made. Its Risk Engine automates transaction reviews, which reduces review times by 30%, according to the company.
  > Typically, such fraud detection is measured by how it limits losses. But van der Does said it's just as important to measure additional transactions that are approved.
  > He used the example of an Israeli software developer who works in New York and sends a purchase to Europe with a credit card issued in Israel. There's a good chance that such a transaction might be flagged or blocked. But with AI able to process more detail, it might realize that the developer is just sending flowers and the transaction is probably fine.

  > Anthropic's massive compute needs align with growing profit pressure at xAI, Elon Musk's AI unit. xAI has rented compute to rivals since May, and its June IPO made the push for revenue even more urgent, the New York Times reports. Anthropic is now xAI's biggest customer with a contract worth roughly $3.1 billion a month. Google spends $800 million. Either deal can be canceled with 90 days' notice.
  > xAI now accounts for over half of xAI's total revenue. Insiders say the company had to finish new data centers by October to fill Anthropic's orders, and Musk says the Claude maker wants to rent even more.
  > In August, Musk pushed engineers in a group chat for "revenue per GPU,"frustrated in part that xAI's own models can barely compete. He reportedly renamed an internal chat "Sell compute because we can't compete."
  > xAI is cutting or restructuring its own AI projects to match that shift. Unit chief Mike Nicolls told staff in November that the 60-person team behind the Grok Imagine image and video generator would be disbanded. An internal memo pointed to critical business priorities. xAI shut down its AI avatars in September, and OpenAI also killed its Sora video model over capacity limits.

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6.
  > Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a bl o g post. The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text.
  > Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options.
  > Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes. While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points.
  > ### Capabilities emerge at distinct perplexity thresholds
  > Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math.
  > The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Astra, plus an internal model at around 0.73.
  > ### OpenAI's models deliver math breakthroughs in a Slack thread
  > OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal"to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread.
  > Those results include a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the Millennium Prize problems, though it hasn't been fully verified yet. The same goes for the proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis found by Claude and an Anthropic researcher. Pachocki thinks...

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.”
  > “Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.”
  > The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors.
  > xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however.
  > Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages.

### AWS 首席执行官马特·加曼 (Matt Garman) 表示，人工智能安全不能依赖于“紧急制动”，数十年安全系统背后的相同工程原理也适用于人工智能

- 核心摘要: 亚马逊负责任的人工智能方法的基础可以在我们的核心领导原则之一中找到：成功和规模带来广泛的责任。数千个自主 AI 代理在 AWS Emulator 中编写了每一行代码，AWS 模拟器是一个新的 AWS 本地模拟器，现已可供下载。第15届re:Invent年度回归

  > Nvidia Corp. reported its quarterly results this week, and contrary to the prevailing narrative, the sky didn’t fall.
  > Revenue more than doubled year-over-year. The Vera Rubin chip platform achieved the fastest product ramp in the company’s history, and management raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to roughly 75%, up from 70%. By all accounts, it was a solid beat and raise.
  > This was Nvidia’s first earnings call without co-founder Jensen Huang, whose resignation as president and chief executive was announced on Nov. 12. Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that the resignation followed the “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” Hours after Huang publicly said he would be willing to return, Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and would not take questions about the circumstances or the board’s ongoing investigation.
  > Colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer who is now also serving as interim CEO, set the tone in her first minute: “Our ambition will not change. Our passion for innovation will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change.”
  > After listening to the call, I believe Nvidia answered the short-term question and left the long-term one open. The company made a convincing case that it can execute without its founder. It has yet to show who decides where it goes next. Here are five things we learned and what they mean for those who buy, budget for or operate artificial intelligence infrastructure.
  > ### 1. The machine will run without the founder
  > The fear going into the call was disruption. The quarter closed before Huang’s exit, so the results can’t settle that. The guidance can, and it went up. Hyperscalers brought Vera Rubin into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell required. The roadmap is set through Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028, and Kress said the supply agreements extend through the end of the decade.
  > She explained that the past month has been “Business as usual.” Kress added, “We’ve engaged with our customers, suppliers and partners. They’re all 100% behind us.” She also noted that TSMC leadership was at Nvidia’s offices this week.
  > I have long held that Nvidia’s moat was never the silicon. It’s the accumulated layers of systems, software and supply chain built around it. The past week was the first real test of that view, and so far, it’s holding. A yearly product cadence this complex runs on thousands of engineers and a supply chain planned years in advance.
  > Asked about talent retention, Kress acknowledged that “there are diverse opinions” among employees while insisting they are “committed to doing their life’s work” at Nvidia. The c...

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Jensen Huang is back, baby, and Wall Street is thrilled.
  > The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars.
  > Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees. Each report chipped away at the company’s value, until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the last month.
  > Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia's board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.”
  > And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back—with some help from the US government. Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return.
  > Many questions remain unanswered. What happens at the conclusion of the board-led investigation into Huang’s behavior? Multiple government agencies and lawmakers are reportedly investigating Huang; given the Trump administration’s aggressive support of the executive, what sort of accountability can anyone reasonably expect?
  > The turmoil has also raised red flags about what happens when so much of the market revolves around one person at one company. Nvidia has massive sway over the wider artificial intelligence ecosystem, due to its deals with and investments in other companies. Last week, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10 percent, in part due to Nvidia’s struggles—the index’s biggest decline since March 2020.
  > On Monday morning, CNBC asked Trump if Nvidia’s influence on the stock market influenced his decision to push for Huang’s return. “Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term,” Trump responded.
  > Trump, who has worked closely with Huang during his second administration, established himself as a vocal supporter of the CEO amidst the recent chaos. Trump told The New York Times that he believed the board responded positively to his argument for Huang’s return because of the stock market dip, with the president suggesting that investors didn’t have much confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress.
  > “I just thought he should be running the company, and I didn’t know it was going to have this kind of an impact,” Trump told The New York Times. “I’ve never seen anything quite like it actually. The stock is up.”
  > According to Trump, however, his decision wasn’t guided so...

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here .
  > Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.
  > Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.
  > This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll , 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).
  > But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.
  > Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is , Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.
  > You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.
  > “Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.
  > The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing ...

  > Anthropic is one of Elon Musk’s biggest competitors in artificial intelligence. It is also one of his biggest customers.
  > Since May, Mr. Musk’s SpaceX has made billions of dollars a month leasing computing power from its data centers to companies like Anthropic and Google. At the same time, SpaceX is developing its own A.I. products, like its chatbot Grok and A.I. agent Grok Bot.
  > Mr. Musk has told employees that SpaceX is falling behind in A.I. development, making it more lucrative to rent the company’s computing power out to rivals than use it to improve its own products, according to three people with knowledge of his comments.
  > But Mr. Musk is frustrated by the situation, the people said. In a group chat with hundreds of engineers at SpaceX’s A.I. unit, he shared data showing the company lagged competitors. And once a week, he has asked some group members to list their work in the chat to justify the use of specialized computer chips, or graphics processing units, which train A.I. systems, the people said.
  > In August, Mr. Musk temporarily changed the group chat name to “Sell compute because we can’t compete,” according to communications viewed by The New York Times. He added a warning to employees who were not using the company’s computing resources wisely: “Anyone wasting GPUs on bullshit while we are failing to compete will be asked to leave immediately, as this constitutes a betrayal of your team.”
  > The tension highlights a central conflict in Mr. Musk’s A.I. push. He started an A.I. company, xAI, a year after OpenAI’s blockbuster release of ChatGPT in 2022, and has spent billions building data centers to catch up. Now, with SpaceX newly public and under pressure to show investors it can turn a profit, Mr. Musk is stuck renting much of that firepower out to the same companies he’s chasing.
  > That has set off a monthslong scramble for resources that has pitted the company’s ambitions — and at times even Mr. Musk’s pet projects — against its balance sheet.
  > The unit, renamed SpaceXSI, now generates more than half of all revenue for SpaceX, which once relied on money from government contracts to send rockets to space. SpaceX highlighted the risks of selling computing power to competitors in a prospectus before going public in June, saying the company’s data center leasing business could “create operational complexity.”
  > Anthropic and Google have each forged deals to lease computing power from SpaceX, with Anthropic’s valued at about $3.1 billion a month and Google’s $800 million a month. These deals could run through 2029, but could also be terminated by either party with 90 days’ notice.

  > Late last week, Mr. Trump decided he wanted to do whatever he could to help Mr. Huang get his old job back, the people said, despite concerns from his own national security agencies about Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman they believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset and who was also believed to be involved in possible illegal smuggling of Nvidia chips into China.

Only a tiny handful of officials at the highest level of the government were aware of these conversations.

Mr. Trump was said to have been thrilled that the plan to restore Mr. Huang was executed without any leaks.
  > In directing Mr. Vance to engage with Mr. Huang and his peers, Mr. Trump was turning to one of the members of his administration with the strongest relationships in Silicon Valley. The vice president is close to some of Mr. Huang’s biggest supporters and admirers, such as David Sacks, the investor and co-chairman of the President’s Council of Advisers on Science and Technology. Mr. Sacks previously served as Mr. Trump’s key adviser on artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency issues.
  > Representatives for Mr. Huang and Mr. Vance declined to comment. A spokesman for Nvidia did not respond to an email seeking comment.
  > On Monday morning, Mr. Trump rejoiced in Nvidia’s action, saying on his social media website Truth Social that the company “made the correct and proper decision.” The president explicitly connected the reinstatement of Mr. Huang to the health of the U.S. economy.
  > “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Mr. Trump wrote.

  > "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones said. Jones will remain chair, and Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, continues as chief financial officer.
  > "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said in the statement. "I can't wait to get back to work."
  > The decision overturns the board's position from last week. "The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said on the company's November 17 earnings call, as Nvidia hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.
  > Hours earlier, Huang had offered to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company "and America." His comeback had drawn support from President Donald Trump and Elon Musk, even as CNBC reported that directors were not considering it.
  > Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. China has denied that she is a spy.
  > The independent directors' committee investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion," Nvidia said, and Huang has said he will cooperate with it.
  > The company also pointed to its new National Security and Export Control Committee, made up of independent directors, and said it is searching for a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the company. Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with government investigations and inquiries.

  > "Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," Warren said.

  > Representative Don Bacon, a Republican, said, "Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high-end computer chips sales to China."
  > Huang separately agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees, slated for December 1.
  > Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell said the Nvidia board "made an irresponsible decision to reinstate Jensen Huang before Congress has even heard from him."
  > She added, "There are serious national security questions that still need to be answered. The board must explain why it was willing to move ahead without those answers."
  > Republican Senator John Cornyn also questioned the board's determination. "No national security risk? Based on what?" Cornyn said on X.
  > Democratic Representative Richard Neal noted the Nvidia board cited "input from senior levels of the United States government" and said "this is one of the many reasons Congress needs to get answers on what exactly is going on here."
  > Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, a potential Democratic presidential candidate, also criticized the decision. "This is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected," Pritzker said.

  > Let’s say you’re Jensen Huang. You (allegedly) cheated on your wife with an alleged Chinese spy, allegedly had an affair with not one, but two subordinates, and (allegedly!) “terrorized” your employees, a series of indiscretions that led to your ouster from what was once the world’s most valuable company. (The stock price has recently taken a tumble, for obvious reasons.) And now you’re back, baby — and all your friends are so eager to congratulate you.
  > Elon Musk, for one, is thrilled.
  > And why wouldn’t he be? As a fellow leather jacket enthusiast who has a checkered history with women — including those who work for him — it’s clear that he and Huang have a lot in common beyond their positions as tech CEOs. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, too, is a man who can relate to Huang’s struggle.
  > Gavin Baker, founder and chief investment officer of Atreides, is so impressed by Huang’s rise from the ashes that he’s going to buy a leather jacket of his own.
  > Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeny chimed in with an oblique reference to Huang’s outerwear.
  > And then there’s billionaire investor Bill Ackman, a real wife guy if there ever was one — but one who, for better or worse, seems to understand that the market comes first.
  > Of course, no one has been more effusive than the man who may have orchestrated it all. President Donald Trump posted his lengthy congratulations to Huang on Truth Social. “I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump wrote. He commended Nvidia’s board for making the “correct and proper” decision in reinstating Huang — a decision that, the board admits, was made with input “from senior levels of the United States government,” who determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no security risk.” Isn’t that great news?
  > Trump expects Huang to make him proud. “I think you’re going to see some tremendous numbers out of this company,” Trump said on CNBC. “I talked to him last night. I said, ‘Jensen, just promise me one thing: You’re going to work hard.’ I spoke to him last night because I knew what was going on.”
  > The market’s reaction may be the most jubilant of all. Per Odd Lots host Joe Weisenthal, NASDAQ-100 futures jumped so quickly that trading was halted. Congratulations to everyone who bought the dip, I guess.

  > Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Huang, saying the company had received assurances from “senior levels of the United States government” that he posed no national security risk after carrying on an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
  > “President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said.
  > Nvidia’s board met late last night, according to a person familiar with the matter, and voted unanimously. Huang’s resignation spurred an outcry from some Silicon Valley figures who called for his return. Semafor had previously reported that a faction of directors had continued to push for him to come back.
  > The anti-Jensen camp was dealt a blow when they learned a leading Huang replacement candidate, Arm CEO Rene Haas, had signed a new contract with Arm extending his employment until 2033, according to another person familiar with some directors’ thinking.
  > “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, who was elevated at the time of Huang’s Nov. 12 ouster to board chairman, said in a statement.
  > The decision comes less than two weeks after Huang stepped down under pressure, and returns Huang to the company he founded in 1993 and built into an AI giant. Huang has also been accused of having an affair with a subordinate.
  > Nvidia’s stock was up nearly 30% in early trading Monday, the biggest jump in more than two decades.

### Z.ai 跟随 OpenAI 进入环路变压器领域，推出全新 750B 旗舰型号

- 原始信源: THE DECODER (https://the-decoder.com/z-ai-follows-openai-into-loop-transformer-territory-with-its-new-750b-flagship-model/)
- 核心摘要: Z.ai 正在将其旗舰模型转向循环架构，该架构的某些层运行两次。该公司希望通过 GLM-5.4 标志着“通用编码”的开始，其中代码还可以生成视频、游戏和 CAD 模型。继 OpenAI 之后，Z.ai 推出了 GLM-5.4，这是其第一个基于环形变压器构建的大型模型
- 核验事实清单:

- 独家研判与技术透视: {'briefing_zh': 'Z.ai 跟随 OpenAI 进入环路变压器领域，推出全新 750B 旗舰型号。 Z.ai 正在将其旗舰模型转向循环架构，该架构的某些层运行两次。该公司希望通过 GLM-5.4 标志着“通用编码”的开始，其中代码还可以生成视频、游戏和 CAD 模型。\n\n继 OpenAI 之后，Z.ai 推出了 GLM-5.4，这是其第一个基于环形变压器构建的大型模型。而标准语言模组。', 'briefing_en': 'Z.ai is moving its flagship model to a loop architecture that runs some of its layers twice. - 深度报道全文精录:
  > Z.ai is moving its flagship model to a loop architecture that runs some of its layers twice. With GLM-5.4, the company wants to mark the start of "Generalized Coding,"where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models.
  > Following OpenAI, Z.ai is introducing GLM-5.4, its first large model built on a loop transformer. While standard language models use each layer once per pass, GLM-5.4 runs a block of shared layers multiple times, refining the intermediate results from the previous pass to make the network deeper without adding parameters. OpenAI has used a similar architecture since GPT-6 Astra. According to Z.ai, the 750-billion-parameter model reaches performance comparable to models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters.
  > The team retrained the GLM-5 base model released in February into a loop model that runs 28 layers twice. Loop models trained from scratch have so far performed worse than models without shared weights under the same compute budget, Z.ai writes.
  > ### Gates and shared caching keep the second pass manageable
  > Converting the model introduces a problem, Z.ai says. If the model simply overwrites intermediate states on each pass, activations grow sharply from round to round, leaving subsequent layers with values outside the range they were trained on.
  > To handle this, GLM-5.4 uses dedicated gates for each token and pass to control how much of the new output flows back into the data stream. According to Z.ai, the model builds context cautiously on the first pass and writes its changes back in full on the second. On difficult tokens, Z.ai says, the first pass steps in more strongly.
  > Because the second pass would otherwise double memory usage, both passes share the KV cache, the temporary memory for previously processed tokens. The second pass stores its own extra values only in a small local window. As a result, Z.ai says, the overhead compared to GLM-5.3 stays manageable even at a 1-million-token context.
  > To save on compute as well, the model uses sparse attention to pick the most relevant earlier tokens upfront rather than scanning the entire context every time, a standard technique. The second pass then reuses that selection from the first instead of making a new one. According to Z.ai, that yields nearly the same results as picking tokens separately on each pass. The company also says the model reaches up to 200 tokens per second off-peak and 70 to 80 tokens per second under load.
  > ### A looped 30B test model beats its baseline with shorter reasoning chains
  > Before rolling out the architecture in its flagship, Z.ai tested it on models with 1, 4, 30, and 750 billion parameters. For a direct comparison, the team used a 30B model built on the same architecture as the large base model. Both versions had the same parameter count, while th...

### 分析：GTA VI 已售出 4490 万份，不包括未售出的零售库存，其中 PS5 占 3370 万份，总收入超过 40 亿美元
- 落地页链接: https://ainewsradar.xyz/zh/news/7f2b4a38051f8399
- 原始信源: Alinea (https://alineaanalytics.substack.com/p/gta-6-sells-449m-copies-makes-40b)
- 核心摘要: 里斯·埃利奥特 / 阿琳娜：
分析：GTA VI 已售出 4490 万份，不包括未售出的零售库存，其中 PS5 占 3370 万份，并产生了 40 亿美元以上的总收入 - 我们深入研究了最大销量的销售预估（没有未售出的零售版）
- 核验事实清单:

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Amazon is reportedly closer to a $7.5 billion deal to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart.
  > That’s according to a report Saturday (Nov. 21) by the Financial Times (FT), citing sources familiar with the matter. The report notes that the purchase of Decart, whose software allows AI models to function more efficiently and free up computer chip capacity, helps Amazon Web Services compete with Nvidia.
  > The sources said the negotiations were at an advanced stage for a deal valuing Decart at roughly $7.5 billion. A deal could come together in the coming days, though talks could still fall apart, the sources added.
  > The FT noted that Amazon debuted its Trainium3 AI chip late last year to compete with Nvidia’s widely used graphics processing units. Decart was an early adopter of those chips.
  > Decart was also reported as a potential acquisition target for Anthropic earlier this year, before that company walked away from the deal.
  > The Wall Street Journal reported on Amazon’s interest in Decart in October. A spokesperson for Amazon declined to comment when reached by PYMNTS.
  > This deal is happening as American tech stocks have fallen into “bear market territory,” the FT report added, logging their worst week since the COVID pandemic due to worries that the AI investment boom had begun to cool.
  > In other AI news, recent PYMNTS Intelligence research shows consumers using the technology for money management in a variety of ways.
  > “They can ask an AI assistant to compare financial products, explain annual fees, look up the meaning of an unfamiliar rate or help draft a message questioning a charge,” PYMNTS wrote in the report “Consumers Ask AI Twice: Which Card and Why the Fee?”
  > “Of those specific tasks, comparing financial products had the broadest reach across generations,” the report added. “Even among baby boomers and seniors who used generative AI (Gen AI) in their personal lives, roughly one in eight used it to compare financial products, while just three in 100 used it to draft a dispute or support message.”
  > The research found that 22.5% of consumers surveyed in September of this year had used Gen AI for money management at least once in the last 12 months, a figure little changed from a year earlier. What distinguished consumers was the extent to which they were using AI already, with close to 80% of power users turning to it for money management, and more than half using it for specific needs like crafting a budget.

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. Experts in China worry that artificial intelligence could make it easier for US forces to detect and destroy Chinese nuclear missiles, according to a New York Times analysis. That would undermine China's deterrence strategy, which relies on a guaranteed second-strike capability.
  > Researchers at the Academy of Military Sciences in Beijing write that AI could shrink US decision-making time from 15 to 30 minutes down to 90 seconds. China currently has about 620 operational warheads, according to the Federation of American Scientists, and is expected to expand its arsenal to roughly 1,000 by 2030. At the same time, Chinese military institutes are studying how AI could make their own weapons harder to intercept, for instance by using AI-controlled flight paths for hypersonic missiles.
  > Experts warn, however, that flawed AI data could trigger dangerous miscalculations during a crisis. That risk proved very real earlier this year, when the US military nearly boarded a Chinese ship based on a false, AI-generated intelligence report. Xi Jinping did discuss nuclear risks at a summit with Trump and Putin, but AI's role in nuclear weapons never came up, according to the report. Despite the growing urgency, the US and China have made almost no progress on talks about AI safeguards in nuclear systems.

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.
  > The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.
  > “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.
  > In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”
  > “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”
  > Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return.
  > “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.
  > The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO.
  > In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it.
  > Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so.

  > CFO Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis, and the stock had tanked during that period. President Donald J. Trump praised the decision on Truth Social, saying the US Attorney General found no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang.   > The US government is also reviewing Nvidia's business dealings. Trump urged the company to keep looking into whether its export control compliance holds up. Nvidia has already set up a dedicated oversight committee for that purpose and is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Huang and the company said they'll continue cooperating with authorities and internal investigators. Nvidia's stock jumped more than 30 percent on the news.

- 深度报道全文精录:
  > Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.”
  > In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social, saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
  > The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair.
  > “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.
  > Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement.
  > Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence, while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom. Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.
